Indian Standard (Part VI) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 January 1972 after the draft finahzed by the Soil Engmeerlng Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engmeermg DivisionCouncil o 2 Sod stabihzation is the alteration of any property of a SOlI to Improve Its engineering performance There are several methods of stabthzation and these may be broadly classified on the basis of treatment given to the SOli (for example dewatering and compaction) process mvolved (for example thermal and electrical) and on addiuves employed (for example asphalt and cement) The choiceofa parttcular method depends on the characteristtcs of the problem on hand For studying m the laboratory the methods and effects of stabihzation certain standard methods oftest for the evaluation of properties of'stabihzedSOlIs and their analysis are required The required standards on methods of test for stabihzed sods are to be published in parts and this part [IS 4332 (Part VI) 1972] lays down the procedure for determmmg the flexural strength of soil cement by the use of a simple beam with third point loading o 3 In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to mternational co ordination among the standards and practtces prevailmg in different countries In addrtlon to relating It to the practices in the field in this country This has been met by basing the standard on the following pubhcations ASTM D1632 63 Making and curmg SOlI cement compression and flexural test specimens in the laboratory American Society for Testing and Matenals USA ASTM D1635 63 Test for flexural strength of sod cement using simple beam WIth third point loading American SOCIety for Testing and Materials USA 04 ThIS edition 11 mcorporates Amendment No 1 (February value observed or calculated IS to be rounded off it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 1960�

1 SCOPE

1 1 This standard covers the procedure for determming the flexural strength of sorl cement by the use of a simple beam with third point loadmg

2 APPARATUS 2 1 For the Preparation of Test Specimen 2 1 1 Moulds- havmg inside dimensions of75 x 75 x 300 mm (Fig 1) The moulds shall be so designed that the specimen may be moulded with ItS Iongitudmal axis 10 a horizontal positron The parts of the moulds shall be tight fittmg and positively held together The sides of the moulds shall be sufficiently rigid to prevent spreadmg or warpmg The mtenor faces of the moulds shall be plane surfaces with a permissible vanauon 10 any 75 mm hne on a surface of 0 05 mm for new moulds and 0075 mm for moulds 10 use The distance between opposite sides shall be 75 � 0 25 mm for new moulds and 75 � 0 4 for moulds 10 use The height of the moulds shall be 75 +8 ~~ mm for both new moulds and moulds in use Four 10 mm spacer bars and top and bottom machined steel plates shall be provided The plates shall fit the mould with a clearance of 0 15 mm on all sides The moulds shall be made of metal having a Rockwell hardness between B80 and B85 2 12 Sieves - 50 mm 20 mm 475 mm 1 18 mm conforming to the requirements errs 460 (Part 1) 1985* 2 1 3 Balances - A balance or scale of capacity 10 kg sensitive to 5 g (Class C beam scale orIS 1433 1965t) and a balance of 1 kg sensitive to 100 mg (Class B beam scale of IS 1433 1965t) 2 1 4 Drying Oven thermostatically controlled capable of mamtammg a temperature of 110 � 5�C for drymg moisture samples 2 1 5 Tampmg Rod - A square end cut 12 mm diameter smooth steel rod 500 mm 10 length 2 1 6 MOIstRoom or Cebtnet - capable of mamtaimng a temperature of 27 � 2�C and relative hunudity of not less than 96 percent for moist curmg specimens 2 2 For Testing Flexural Strength 2 2 1 Testing Machme- The testmg machme may be ofany type havmg sufficient capacity (at least 500 kg) and control to provide the rate of loading prescribed III 5 2 The testmg machme shall be equipped Witha spherically seated head block having a bearing surface of 100 percent of

2 2 2 1 The distance between supports and points of load apphcation shall remain constant for a gIven apparatus 2 2 2 2 The direction of the reactions shall be parallel to the direcnon of the applied load at all times during the test 2 2 2 3 The load should be applied at a umform rate and In such a manner as to avoid shock 2 2 2 4 The directions of loads and reactions may be maintained parallel by use of lmkages rocker bearings and flexure plates Eccentncltyof loadmg can be avoided by use of spherical bearmgs 3 PREPARATION OF MATERIALS 3 1 Materials shall be brought to room temperature

IS 4332 (Part VI) 1972 3 2 Cement - Cement shall be stored In a dry place In moisture proofcontainers preferablymade of metal The cement shall be thoroughly mixed in order that the sample may be uniform throughout the tests It shall be passed through a 1 18 mm IS SIeve and all lumps rejected 3 3 Water - The mixingwater shall be free ofacids alkalies and oils and In general suitable for dnnkmg 34 Soil 3 4 1 The soil sample If damp when received from the field shall be dned unnl It becomesfriable under a trowel Drying may be In air or by use of drying apparatus such that the temperature of the sample does not exceed60�C The aggregations shall be thoroughly broken up In such a manner as to avoid reducing the natural size of individual parncles 3 4 2 An adequate quantity of representative pulverized soil shall be SIeved on the 50 mm 20 mm and 4 75 mm SIeves Any fraction retamed on the 50 mm sieve shall be discarded Fraction passing the 50 mm sieve and retained on the 20 mm SIeve shall be removed and replaced with an equal Weight offraction passing the 20 mm sieve and retained on the 475 mm sieve Soil for replacement shall be obtained from the onglnal sample
NOTE - It is intendedthat these methodsfor makingsoilcementspecimensfor the flexuretest be used primarilywith soil materials having not more than 35 percent soil retained on the 475 mm sieve and not more than 85 percent retained on the 425micronsieve

3 4 3 The fraction passing the 20 mm SIeve and retained In the 475 mm sieve shall be soaked In water for 24 hours removed and surface dried The absorption properties of this fraction shall be determined In accordanceWIthIS 2386 (Part III) 1963* 344 A 100g sample of the soil passing the 475 mm sieve shall be taken and dned In the drying oven to constant weight and the moisture content of the sample determined to permit calculation of the quantity of water that shall be added to the soil cement mixture to bring It to the proper moisture content for moulding specimens 3 4 5 A representative sample of sufficient quantity to make three flexure test specimens shall be taken of the soil passIng the 475 mm sieve and also of the fraction passing the 20 mm sieve and retained on the 4 75 mm SIeve prepared as describedin 3 4 1 342 and 343
"Methodsof test for aggregatesfor concrete Part III Speciflc gravity density voids absorptionand bulking

IS 4332 (Part VI) 1972 3 5 Weighing Materials - The designed quantities of soil passing the 4 75 mm SIeveand of aggregate passing the 20 mm SIeveand retained on the 475 mm sieve shall be weighed to the nearest 5 g The designed quantity of cement shall be weighed to the nearest gram and the designed quantity of water shall be measured to the nearest milhlltre 4 PREPARATION OF TEST SPECIMEN 4 1 Mixing Materials 4 1 1 General - Soil cement shall be mixed either by hand or In a suitable laboratory mixer In batches of such SIze as to leave ten percent excess after moulding test specimens ThIS material shall be protected against loss of moisture and a representative part of It shall be weighed and dried In the drying oven to constant weight to determine the actual moisture content of the soil cement mixture When the soil cement mixture contams aggregate retained on the 475 mm SIeve the sample for moisture determmation shall weigh at least 500 g and shall be weighed to the nearest gram If the nuxture does not contain aggregate retained on the 4 75 mm SIeve the sample shall weighat least 100 g and shall be weighedto the nearest 0 1 g 4 1 2 Hand Mtxtng - The batch shall be mixed In a clean damp metal pan or on top of a steel table with a blunt bnck layer s trowel USingthe followingprocedures a) Calculated amount of water to give moisture content 2 percent less than the required final moisture content should be added to the soil passing 4 75 mm IS Sieve thoroughly mixed and kept In a sealed container to aVOId moisture loss overmght for uniform distnbution of moisture b) The additional water required for brmging the moisture to the required level should be calculated The calculated weight of the moist soil and cement required for making the specimens should be mixed thoroughly The remaining quantity of water to make up to the required moisture content of the soil cement mixture should be added and thoroughly mixed c) The saturated surface dry coarse fraction of the soil shall be added and the entire batch mixed until the coarse fraction IS uniformly distributed throughout the batch 4 1 3 MachineMixmg - The sequence specified for hand mixingshall be followed To eliminate segregation machine mixed soil cement shall be deposited In a clean damp metal pan and remixed by trowel
NOTE- The operationof mixingand compacting test specimens shall be continuous and the elapsedtime betweenthe additionof water and flnal compaction shall not exceed30 minutes

IS 4332 (Part VI) 1972

4 2 Size of Specimens - Flexuretest specimens shall be rectangular beamswith a length as tested at least 50 mmgreater than three nmes the depth ThIS procedure providesforbeams75 x 75 x 300mm but the same procedure maybe used for moulding smalleror larger specimens 4 3 Moulding Specimens 4 3 1 The test specimens shall be formed with the longitudinal axis horizontal The mouldparts shall be hghtly oiledand assembledwith sides and ends separated from the base plate by the 10 mm spacer bars one placedat eachcornerofthe mould 4 3 2 Divide into three equal batches a predetermmed weight of umformly mixedsoil cement to make a beam of the designeddensity Placeonebatchofthe material 10 the mouldand levelbyhand Whenthe soil cementcontainsaggregateretainedon the 4 15 mmSIeve carefully spadethe mIX aroundthe sidesofthe mouldwitha thin spatula Compact the sod cementmittallyfromthe bottomupbysteadilyandfirmlyforcing (withhttle Impact) a square end cut 12mm diameter smoothsteel rod repeatedlythroughthe mixturefromthe topdownto the pomt ofrefusal Approximately 90roddingsdistnbuted umformly overthe crosssection of the mouldare required take care so as not to leave holes 10 clayey soil cementmixtures Levelthis layerofcompacted soil cementbyhand and placeand compact layerstwoand three 10 an identicalmanner The specimenat this time shall be approximately 95 mm high 4 3 3 Place the top plate of the mould 10 positlon and remove the spacer bars Obtain final compaction WIth a static load applied by the compression machineor compression frame until the height of 75 mm IS reached 4 3 4 Immediately after compaction carefullydismantlethe mouldand remove the specimen ontoa smooth ngld wood or sheet metal pallet
NOTE- A suggestedmethodforremoving the specimen fromthe mouldIsto remove first the top and then the sides and end plates or the mould The specimen Is then resting on the bottomplate or the mould The flat raceor a carryingpallet Is then placed against one side or the specimen and then the bottom mould plate the specimenand the palletare rotated90' so that the specimen rests on Its sideon the pallet The bottommouldplate Isthen carefullyremoved

4 4 Curing the Specimens - Cure the specimens on pallets 10 the moist roomand protect from free water for the specified moist curing period Generallythe specimenwill be tested in the moist condition directlyafter removalfromthe moistroom
NOTE- Otherconditioning procedures suchas soakingIn water air dryingor oven drying alternate wetting and drying or alternate freezlngand thawtng may be specltled after an Initial moist curing period Curing and conditioning procedures shall be givenIndetail Inthe report

IS 4332 (Part VI) 1972 44 1 Flexural test of moist cured specimens shall be made as soon as practicable after removing from the moist room and during the period between removal from the moist room and testing the specimens shall be kept moist by a wet burlap or blanket covering
4 5 Report - The report on the preparation of specimens shall include the following
a) b) c) d) e) t) Gradation of soil as received and as used In making specimens Specimen identiflcatron number Designed moisture content Designed oven dry density Designed cement content Actual moisture content g) Actual oven dry density h) Actual cement content and J) Details of curing and conditiorung periods

5 PROCEDURE FOR FLEXURAL TEST 5 1 Turn the specimen on Its SIde WIth respect to Its moulded position (with the onginal top and bottom surfaces as moulded perpendicular to the testmg machine bed) and centre It on the lower half round steel supports WhICh shall have been spaced apart a distance of three times the depth of the beam Place the load applying block assembly In contact With the upper surface of the beam at the third points between the supports Carefully align the centre of the beam WIth the centre of thrust of the spherically seated head block of the machine As this block IS brought to bear on the beam loading assembly rotate ItS movable portion gently by hand so that umform seating is obtained 5 2 Apply the load continuously and WIthout shock A screw power testmg machine WIth the moving head operating at approximately 1 2 mm/min when the machine is running idle may be used WIth hydraulic machines adjust the loading to such a constant rate that the extreme fibre stress ISWIthin the llrruts of 7 � 0 4 kglcm2/mm Record the total load at failure of the specimen to the nearest 5 kg 6 MEASUREMENTS OF SPECIMENS AFTER TEST 6 1 Make measurements to the nearest 0 2 mm to determine the average WIdthand depth of the specimens at the section of failure
